Large diameter bosses/shafts (r=10–57mm) forming main load-bearing sections

primarySuggestion.name: 38MnVS6 Microalloyed Forging Steel
primarySuggestion.reasoning: Thick, dense, complex solid (fill ratio 0.092 driven by internal geometry not thin shell) with bosses/shafts up to 57mm radius, multiple bores and threads — classic profile of a forged automotive drivetrain/suspension component (knuckle/arm/hub-type part). Per guidance, thick-section forged parts of this nature default to steel rather than aluminium absent an explicit lightweighting signal. 38MnVS6 is a precipitation-hardening microalloyed steel purpose-built for hot closed-die forging without post-forge heat treatment, common in this part class.

processRecommendations.reasoning: User-forced ground truth; part geometry (thick bosses, moderate free-form blending, high strength requirement implied by drivetrain-type shape) suits closed-die forging at 200k/yr volume, followed by machining of holes/threads.
21 holes, threaded features, and 3 machining setups are required after forging to achieve final bores/threads; bottom-up CNC estimate used verbatim.

manufacturabilityRisks.description: Numerous undercut faces relative to single draw direction cannot be forged in one blow; will require die re-orientation, split-die design, or secondary machining to form these features.
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Re-orient parting line to minimize undercuts or convert undercut features to post-forge machined details.

manufacturabilityRisks.description: Very high variance in wall/section thickness (0.45mm to 170mm) risks incomplete die fill, cold shuts, and flow-line discontinuities in thin regions adjacent to massive bosses.
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Add fillets/ribs to smooth section transitions and add draft to ease metal flow into thin zones.

manufacturabilityRisks.description: 21 holes plus threads cannot be forged net-shape and require a dedicated multi-setup machining line, adding cost and cycle time at 200k/yr volume.
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Consolidate hole operations on one setup where possible; consider coining pilot holes in the forging to reduce drilling stock removal.

manufacturabilityRisks.description: High B-spline face content increases die-sinking (CNC) time and inspection complexity for the forging die cavity.
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Simplify blended surfaces to standard radii/fillets where functionally permissible to reduce die cost.

dfmIssues.description: 44 undercut faces conflict with a single Z-axis draw direction typical of closed-die forging.
dfmIssues.impact: Requires split dies, side-relief inserts, or extra machining — increases tooling cost by 15–25% and lead time.
dfmIssues.fix: Reorient part or split the die along a plane that eliminates most undercuts; move remaining undercuts to post-forge machining.

dfmIssues.description: Boss radii up to 57mm adjacent to sections down to 0.45mm nominal create abrupt metal-flow gradients in the die cavity.
dfmIssues.impact: Risk of laps, cold shuts, and incomplete fill leading to scrap rates >5% at start-of-run.
dfmIssues.fix: Increase fillet radii at boss-to-web transitions and add generous draft (≥7°) to aid metal flow.

dfmIssues.description: Threads and close-tolerance bores cannot be forged net-shape and require full secondary machining across 3 setups.
dfmIssues.impact: Adds ~0.67hr machining + 0.75hr setup per part, dominating unit cost at high volume.
dfmIssues.fix: Pre-form pilot holes in the forging to reduce stock removal; fixture design to combine setups.

dfmIssues.description: High proportion of blended/organic surfaces increases 5-axis die-sinking time and die polishing cost.
dfmIssues.impact: Die cost and lead time increase 10–20% versus a simpler faceted geometry.
dfmIssues.fix: Simplify non-functional blended surfaces to standard radii/fillets to reduce die-sinking time and polishing effort.

sanityWarnings.message: Machining time 0.67 h looked machined-from-solid; a 8.1 kg near-net forging part only needs finish machining — capped to 0.67 h.

dfmIssues.description: Web 0.45 mm below closed-die minimum 3 mm — Thin webs cool fast and resist metal flow — incomplete fill, forging laps and excessive die pressure/wear.
dfmIssues.impact: Web 0.45 mm below closed-die minimum 3 mm
dfmIssues.fix: Thicken the web to ≥ 3 mm, or move to a lower-web process (precision 1.5 mm / cold 1 mm).

dfmIssues.description: Draft -1° below recommended 3° — Insufficient die draft prevents clean part release — galling, ejection cracks and rapid die wear.
dfmIssues.fix: Add ≥ 3° draft on impression walls (deep cavities need 5–7°). Precision/warm forging can run reduced draft with ejectors.

deterministicAnalysis.aiExplanation:
Derived deterministically for forging from the measured geometry. No AI call was made; every figure below is arithmetic on a measurement or a library lookup, and each states its own basis.

  • forging.projectedAreaCm2 = 187.6 — parting-plane silhouette: bbox face × √fill for a solid, bbox face for a shell [geometry, forge-proj-area]
  • forging.shapeComplexity = moderate — 76 free-form face(s), 44 undercut face(s), 364 faces total [geometry, forge-shape]
  • forging.strokesToForm = 8 — blows to fill the impression, from the measured shape [geometry, forge-strokes]
  • forging.timePerBlowSec = 10 — ram travel + dwell per blow on a mechanical press [rule, forge-time-per-blow]

Still open (1):
  • What is this part made of? — A CAD file carries shape, not substance. We measured 1037 cm³ exactly, but the same solid weighs 2.80 kg in aluminium and 8.14 kg in steel. Nothing in the geometry distinguishes them, and guessing wrong moves the material cost several-fold.
analysisLimitations: Unanswered: What is this part made of?

DFM checks ran against the measured geometry. Checks that need a drawing callout — tolerances, which face is critical, whether a weld line is in a load path — did not run, so this list is a floor and not a ceiling.
